findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are stored in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables, readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration and committed to source control.

The Lambda function does not specify a kms_key_arn, so environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default service-owned key rather than a customer-managed KMS key with controlled key policy and rotation.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS.
No vpc_config is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group-based egress control, providing a data exfiltration path.

findings.issue_category: missing permissions boundary and confused deputy protection
findings.description: The Lambda execution role's trust policy allows any lambda.amazonaws.com principal to assume it with no aws:SourceAccount/aws:SourceArn condition and no permissions boundary, weakening cross-account confused-deputy protection and privilege guardrails.
